title: Refine table affordances: sticky guides, clip-over previews, and smooth density transitions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a cohesive set of UX patterns and production-ready assets for the table component to improve discoverability and control of column resizing, sorting/filtering, and density changes. Focus areas: 1) sticky column guide lines and snap hints to make resizing precise on high-density tables; 2) clip-over hover previews that reveal clipped cell content without breaking virtualization performance; 3) smooth density transitions (a 'density glide') so users can move between compact/comfortable modes without layout jank. Work includes interaction specs, accessibility requirements, and handoff-ready Figma components and tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Design specs for sticky column guide lines with snap magnetism documented and approved by Eng and PM
Clip-over hover preview behaviour defined, with keyboard-accessible alternative and a performance budget (no >10ms additional per-row cost in our perf test harness)
Density glide prototypes demonstrating smooth interpolation across at least three density presets (compact, standard, comfortable) and clear token mapping for spacing/line-height
Figma components and tokens delivered, variant-ready, with clear naming and token usage notes
Accessibility checklist completed: focus order, keyboard resize handle, aria descriptions for clipped content previews, contrast checks for guide lines
Engineering acceptance: small demo PR integrating design tokens and the hover preview stub (link in 'links')
Design review approved and a rollout plan added to the Console roadmap (release tag)
design_decisions: Use a thin, high-contrast sticky guide line that appears on column hover/drag rather than persistent grid lines to reduce visual noise
Adopt 'magnetic snapping' to common column widths with an optional modifier key to temporarily disable snapping for fine-grained control
Implement clip-over hover previews as a portal that layers above the virtualized viewport to avoid reflow; provide keyboard invocation via 'Enter' on focused cell
Implement density glide by interpolating spacing tokens rather than hard-swapping classes to minimize layout shifts and reflows
Keep default behaviour conservative on mobile (no hover previews) and provide an explicit preview action in the row context menu
tradeoffs: Clip-over previews require a layering solution that sits outside the virtualization window. Pros: no rerender of virtual window and instant reveal. Cons: additional complexity in z-order management and potential accessibility edge cases.

Magnetic snapping simplifies resizing for most users but can be frustrating for power users; we propose a modifier key (Ctrl/Cmd) to disable snapping rather than a global setting to minimize UI surface.
Interpolating tokens for density reduces visual jank but increases the complexity of token mapping and may require engineering work to support fractional pixel spacing on some browsers.

Adding keyboard preview flow improves accessibility but needs careful UX to avoid accidental activation; chosen pattern ties preview activation to focus+Enter rather than simple focus to reduce false positives.
